content_blocks.text: The UK is an independent member of the World Trade Organisation Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO GPA).
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

content_blocks.text: A new Scottish Policy Note SPPN 5/2023 has been released to communicate the WTO GPA procurement thresholds that will be in place from 1 st January 2024 until 31 st December 2025.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

content_blocks.text: When you calculate the estimated value of your contract you must include VAT (if applicable) at the appropriate rate for your contract (or apply the standard UK VAT rate of 20%). More information is detailed below.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

content_blocks.text: The threshold values for regulated procurements remain at £50,000 for goods and services.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

content_blocks.text: If you are unable to estimate the value of a contract that contract will be explicitly made subject to the procurement rules.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

content_blocks.text: Unless you can show that your contract has no VAT or a lower rate of VAT, it is recommended best practice to add 20% to the net estimated value of your contract. 20% is the current standard rate of VAT. Adding this standard rate will:
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

content_blocks.text: Reduce the risk of underestimating the contract value
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

content_blocks.text: ensure you follow the correct procurement route and advertising requirements in line with the correct procurement thresholds
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

content_blocks.text: If VAT is applicable you must include an allowance in your calculation of the estimated value of the contract to determine whether the contract equals or exceeds the new threshold values.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

How to Calculate the Estimated Value of your Contract

content_blocks.text: The estimated value of your contract must include the full lifetime of your contract (including any possible extension periods) plus VAT (if applicable).
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How to Calculate the Estimated Value of your Contract

content_blocks.text: For example, if your contract is for 3 years plus a possible 1 year extension at an estimated value of £50k per annum, this is:
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How to Calculate the Estimated Value of your Contract

content_blocks.text: 4 years (3 years + 1 year extension) x £50k = £200k estimated contract value
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How to Calculate the Estimated Value of your Contract

content_blocks.text: If your contract is subject to VAT add a 20% allowance for VAT i.e £200k + £40 = £240k
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How to Calculate the Estimated Value of your Contract

content_blocks.text: If your contract is not subject to VAT the total estimated value of your contract = £200k
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How to Calculate the Estimated Value of your Contract

content_blocks.text: In both instances the advertised contract value should be £200k i.e. exclude VAT.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How to Calculate the Estimated Value of your Contract

content_blocks.text: WTO GPA procurement thresholds change every 2 years i.e. the next threshold change will occur on 1 January 2026, to allow for currency fluctuations.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value

Contract Notice and Contract Award Notices

content_blocks.text: Net values should continue to be used for Contract Notices and/or Contract Award Notices i.e. you should continue to exclude VAT in these circumstances.

How Do I Know if VAT Applies to my Contract?

content_blocks.text: If you have any queries about specific VAT rates for your contract you should seek advice from your own legal and finance departments.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How Do I Know if VAT Applies to my Contract?

content_blocks.text: Please find below some guidance on how this may apply to your contract:
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How Do I Know if VAT Applies to my Contract?

content_blocks.text: VAT Exempt or Zero Rate VAT Contracts
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How Do I Know if VAT Applies to my Contract?
VAT Exempt or Zero Rate VAT Contracts

content_blocks.text: If all of the contract’s subject matter is exempt from VAT or zero rated VAT, then you do not need to include VAT when calculating the estimated value of the contract.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How Do I Know if VAT Applies to my Contract?
VAT Exempt or Zero Rate VAT Contracts

content_blocks.text: You must be careful to ensure that this is the case for all elements of the contract.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How Do I Know if VAT Applies to my Contract?
VAT Exempt or Zero Rate VAT Contracts

content_blocks.text: VAT Recoverable Contracts
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How Do I Know if VAT Applies to my Contract?
VAT Exempt or Zero Rate VAT Contracts
VAT Recoverable Contracts

content_blocks.text: If VAT is initially payable but later reclaimed it must be included in the calculation of the estimated value of the contract.
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
How Do I Know if VAT Applies to my Contract?
VAT Exempt or Zero Rate VAT Contracts
VAT Recoverable Contracts

content_blocks.text: It is recommended best practice to add 20% to your estimated contract value where you believe that your contract, or an element of your contract may be subject to VAT, but cannot be certain of the rate that should be applied. 20% is recommended as this is currently the standard rate of VAT in the UK. Adding this standard rate reduces the risk of underestimating the contract value and helps ensure your contract is advertised correctly
heading_path: How to Use the Threshold Values and Calculate Your Estimated Contract Value
